summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Edgbaston commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 287/10 (89.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 274/10 (75.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 5-Wicket Spell: Ishant Sharma (5/50), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Virat Kohli delivered a masterclass for India (200 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (England 52%) and allowing England to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, India faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. England's bowling unit, bolstered by SM Curran (87 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing England won by 31 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: England's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While India produced fighting phases, England won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
